prerequisites.description: Minimal regularity / flow-completeness needed for jet transport to be defined for a vector field at all, before 'for all vector fields' is a well-typed quantifier.
What plays the role of a Weil algebra for a non-Weil-lift 'extension' — needed before asking whether jet transport makes sense outside Weil lifts.

Whether composing two Weil-functor extensions yields another construction of the same kind (e.g. indexed by a tensor/fiber-product Weil algebra) — needed for nested/iterated extensions to be a well-typed single hypothesis rather than 'test the two-fold case at every depth'.

What formally constitutes 'respecting a change of isomorphism between same-dimension Weil algebras' for a method — the action and the invariance notion must be pinned down before this is a testable hypothesis.

digest.description: Maximal vector-field class rather than an arbitrary large-but-unspecified one
digest.sharpens: Replaces an unspecified 'large enough class' quantifier with a canonical extremal class, removing an arbitrary choice from the hypothesis.

digest.description: Maximal Weil-algebra class rather than excluding only the trivial algebra
digest.sharpens: Forces an explicit description of the full class of Weil algebras covered, closing off silent restriction to a convenient subclass.

digest.description: Non-Weil-lift extensions as candidate carriers of jet transport
digest.sharpens: Would widen the classification to distinguish methods on constructions Weil theory doesn't see, a genuinely different axis from Weil-algebra size.
Adds a parameter-direction test class, ruling out methods that are only parameter-agnostic by accident.
Adds a time-direction test class, forcing the autonomous/non-autonomous distinction into the open.

digest.description: Extension with respect to initial value
digest.sharpens: Closest to classical variational-equation jet prolongation; most likely to have literature precedent to check the hypothesis against.
Replaces one global Weil algebra with a fibered per-coordinate choice, forcing compatibility with mixed-order jet structure.
Tests stability of jet transport under composition, strictly stronger than any single-axis version.

digest.description: Iterated/unbounded nesting of IV, time, and parameter extensions
digest.sharpens: Only sharpens beyond item 8 once composition-closure (prerequisite P3) is settled; otherwise not yet a distinct hypothesis.

digest.description: Equivariance/naturality under isomorphisms of same-dimension, non-canonically-isomorphic Weil algebras
digest.sharpens: Surfaces a candidate added hypothesis excluding methods that are extension-compatible only for one coordinate choice on the Weil algebra.

directions.description: State and test jet transport for the maximal class of vector fields (relative to some fixed regularity/completeness threshold to be determined) rather than a fixed convenient test class, for the standard Weil-lift extensions.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] a maximal-class reformulation is the cheapest global strengthening and can be tried on the existing Weil-lift definition without any new construction.

directions.description: State and test jet transport specifically for the initial-value extension (Weil lift along the initial condition, e.g. variational-equation-type prolongation), as the template single-axis extension case.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] initial-value jet extension is the most classically grounded of the parameter/time/IV triple, so is most likely to have an existing definition to anchor the claim against.

directions.description: State and test jet transport for a two-fold nested extension (one Weil-lift extension composed with a second, distinct one, e.g. initial-value extension followed by time extension), stopping short of unbounded iteration.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] testing the first non-trivial composition case exposes whether jet transport is stable under composition without first needing the composition-closure fact that unbounded iteration (item 9 in digest) would require.

directions.description: State and test jet transport under a per-coordinate fibered extension, where each coordinate of the original system is Weil-lifted independently rather than the system as a whole sharing one global Weil algebra.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] a fibered/product extension is a strictly more general object than a single global Weil algebra, so if the property survives it is evidence the classification does not depend on treating coordinates uniformly.

directions.description: Add an equivariance hypothesis to jet transport: require the method to respect isomorphisms between Weil algebras of equal dimension (not merely the algebras' dimension/order), and test whether this is already implied or is a genuinely new constraint.
directions.heuristic: [HEURISTIC] equal dimension does not imply canonical isomorphism, so a method compatible with one presentation of the Weil algebra need not be compatible with another — testing this directly targets where an implicit extra hypothesis may be hiding.
